"All is created by mind alone. Upon hearing this, Vasubandhu attained sudden awakening and understood the correct principles of the Mahāyāna. He repented his former slanders and felt deep remorse, wondering what could now remedy it.
Tracing the root of his transgression, he found it lay solely with his tongue; he then rose, took up a sharp blade, and intended to cut it off.
Asanga perceived this from afar, extended his arm, and seized him, admonishing him, saying: "Your awakening to the Mahāyāna is indeed due to..."

"It is time. Previously you used your tongue to disparage; now you ought to use your tongue to praise, so as to compensate for that transgression. Furthermore, if you sever your tongue and remain silent, what benefit would there be?

Vasubandhu accepted this instruction and desisted. Subsequently, upon meeting his former teacher, he listened attentively to the compassionate instructions and composed the Mahāyāna-śāstra, the Śata-śāstra, the Pañcaskandhaka-śāstra, the Viṃśatikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra, the Triṃśikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra, and other such treatises. There was no [limit].
Dharmapāla, having fully mastered the Mahāyāna, entered the Samādhi of Dharma-Light within the Great Lecture Hall in the kingdom of Ayodhyā.

At night, he ascended to the Tuṣita Heaven Palace and requested the Holy Maitreya to expound the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra*, extensively elucidating the meaning of the five divisions and seventeen stages (*bhūmis*).
Asanga composed a two-fascicle treatise on the meaning of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* based on eighteen topical sections;
Vasubandhu composed a three-fascicle treatise based on the resolution of twenty-seven doubts.

The *Record of the Dharma-Abiding by the Divine Monk’s Acceptance of Offerings* states: In the Kingdom of Siṃhala, there was an arhat named Kalyāṇamitra who was fully endowed with the eight liberations, the three knowledges, and the six supernormal powers.
He addressed the great assembly, saying: "The Tathāgata has previously already taught the *Dharmasthiti-sūtra*. After the Buddha's parinirvāṇa..."
At the time of his parinirvāṇa, he entrusted the Unsurpassed Dharma to the sixteen great Arhats and their retinues, commanding them to protect and uphold it so that it would not perish or disappear.
He further commanded that their bodies serve as true fields of merit for all donors, enabling those who give to obtain great rewards.
He then spoke the names of the sixteen Arhats; the first was Piṇḍola-bharadvāja.
1. Raivata; 2. Kanakavatsa; 3. Kanakabharadvāja; 4. Subhadra;
5. Nakula; 6. Bhadra; 7. Kaliṅga; 8. Vajraputra; 9. Śubhaka; 10. Paṃtaka; 11. [The eleventh].
Rāhula; the twelfth, Nāgasena; the thirteenth, Aṅgada; the fourteenth, Vanavāsī; the fifteenth, Aśvita;

and the sixteenth, Cūḍapanthaka—all of whom possessed the three types of clear knowledge and the six supernormal powers—by virtue of the Buddha’s command, used their supernormal powers to go to the monastery and remain in places such as the walking paths.
They distribute bedding, robes, medicine, food, and drink as offerings to the assembly of monks.

These Arhats and their retinues disperse and proceed according to their needs, manifesting various forms; they conceal their noble appearance and blend in with ordinary people, receiving offerings in secret.
Thus they act as true fields of merit for all donors, enabling them to obtain supreme rewards and ensuring that the True Dharma endures for a long time.
For the benefit of all sentient beings in the world,
the *Sūtra of the Ten Great Vidyārājas and the Ten Wrathful Vidyārājas* states: "The Tathāgata Mahāvairocana eternally abides in the samādhi of peaceful bliss."
The Ground. Never departing from great wisdom, great practice, and great compassion and mercy in the salvation of sentient beings, he addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"I shall now emit light rays, desiring to proclaim the Great King of Tantras of Yoga, the Great Net of Illusory Transformation of Great Wisdom and Great Sovereignty;
the practice of the skillful means of Vajra-great-wisdom, which is the most supreme among all that is produced by the ocean of all meanings. Regarding all...
The supreme among teachings, the most supreme of all, which skillfully establishes sentient beings in bliss and leads them into the wisdom of skillful means;

the Great Sovereign Vajra Savior, the Samādhi of Great Bliss Vajra. Having emerged from this meditative absorption, he emitted great radiance that illuminated the entire assembly, and spoke the visualization of the King of Illumination for the Samaya Maṇḍala of the Great Yoga of the Net of Great Māyā.
The Ritual Method for Visualization: First, the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Yamāntaka; second, the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Aparājita;
third, the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Padmāntaka; fourth, the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Vighnāntaka;
fifth, the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Acala; sixth, the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Takkirāja.
1. Vidyārāja; 2. Vilokanātha Vidyārāja; 3. Mahābalavīra Vidyārāja; 4. Mahābala Vidyārāja; 5. Mahāpracaṇḍa Vidyārāja; 6. Mahācaṇḍa Vidyārāja; 7.
Nīladaṇḍa Krodhavīra Vidyārāja; 8. Mahābalamahākrodhavīra Vidyārāja; 9. Śumbha Mahākrodhavīra Vidyārāja; 10. Vajrapātāla Mahākrodhavīra Vidyārāja.
These ten great krodhavīra vidyārājas each have three faces, with three eyes on each face, and all bear a Buddha upon their heads. By...
Wearing a tiger skin as a garment and a skull as a crown, with the topknot of hair standing upright, the practitioner of vidyādhara, visualizing according to the ritual method,
will achieve all practices and vows without exception.
According to the traditions of the various devas who protect the Dharma: first, the Great Brahmā Heavenly King, the sovereign of the Sahā world, whose commands are uniquely honored;
second, Śakra Devendra, the king of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the lord of the earth-dwelling worlds; and third, Vaiśravaṇa, the great yakṣa lord who protects the northern quarter.
1. The Honored Deva Śakra; 2. The World-Protecting Gandharva King Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the east;
3. The World-Protecting Kumbhāṇḍa King Virūḍhaka in the south; 4. The World-Protecting Mahoraga King Virūpākṣa in the west; 5.
The Vajrapāṇi Guhyapada, who vowed to become a powerful Malla to personally subdue the hostile māras; 6. The Sovereign Lord of Exalted Splendor.
1. Mahesvara, who dwells in the Heaven of the Pinnacle of Form (*rūpāvacara-śikhara*) and presides over the nine and twenty-eight classes of spirits and deities;

2. Vaiśravaṇa, the Great General (*mahāsenāpati*), who leads the various hosts of spirits and deities; 3. The Goddess of Great Eloquence (*mahāpratisarā-mahājñānaskandha-mahāpratibhāna-devī*), who can bestow the great mass of wisdom and great eloquence of *dhāraṇīs*;
4. The Goddess of Great Merit (*mahāpuṇya-devī*), who grants the fulfillment of whatever one seeks; 5. Veda, who with earnest concern protects the fourfold assembly and the three continents.
13. The Celestial Deity who Increases and Manifests Transcendent Realization; 14. The Earth Deity of Firm Ground, whose Merits are Solid; 15.

The Bodhi Tree Deity, who provides shade over the site of enlightenment and whose cause and effect mutually adorn one another; 16. The Ghost-Mother Deity, who gives birth to the kings of ghosts and protects men and women;
17. The Mārīcī Deity, who travels before the sun and moon to save those from the calamities of war.
The Son of Heaven of the Solar Palace, who with a hundred brilliant rays benefits sentient beings and with a thousand lights dispels darkness;

the Son of Heaven of the Lunar Palace, the King of Constellations among the eighteen stellar lords, whose cool radiance illuminates the night; and Sāgara-rāja, the Lord of the Many Dragons, who upholds the Dharma-treasure of the secret storehouse.

The twenty lords of the hidden and dark realms act as the lords of hell, King Yama; they all protect the nation and pacify the people, protect the teachings, protect those who practice the path, and cause the True Dharma to circulate.

The *Śāsanānvaya-dharmagupta-avadāna-sūtra* states: The Buddha entrusted the True Dharma to Mahākāśyapa; Kāśyapa, in turn, transmitted it through successive generations until it reached the Venerable One named Siṃha.
He performed great Buddhist activities in the kingdom of Kaśmīra and, with his saṃghāṭī robe...
He entrusted it to his disciple Vasiṣṭha, saying: "The Tathāgata’s Treasury of the Eye of the True Dharma is now transmitted to you.

You should protect it so that it may universally moisten all beings until the end of time. He spoke in verse: "When the true teaching of knowledge and vision is expounded, Knowledge and vision are both the mind itself.
One should know that knowledge and vision are right here; Knowledge and vision are this very moment. Such a Dharma is a great bright lamp, Capable of illuminating the world."
[It is] the darkness of ignorance in the interim. For this reason, all the noble sages protect one another, entrust themselves to one another, and constantly turn the wheel of Dharma.
They bring great benefit to all sentient beings, blocking off the evil paths and opening the way to the realms of humans and devas.
Until finally, when this Dharma decays and vanishes and the noble sages have disappeared, no one will be able to establish it; thus the world’s darkness is dispelled and light is created.
Those who commit evil deeds and practice the ten unwholesome paths will, at the end of their lives, mostly fall into the three miserable realms or the eight difficult conditions.
Therefore, the wise should carefully observe that the unsurpassed and supreme Dharma possesses great merit; it is subtle, profound, and inconceivable.
It is like a merchant who wishes to cross the great ocean: only by boarding a ship can he successfully reach the other side. All sentient beings are likewise [dependent upon this Dharma].
It is likewise so. Those who wish to emerge from the great ocean of birth and death within the triple world must rely upon the Dharma-ship to attain liberation.
A true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) provides great benefit, rescuing one from all suffering and distress and unraveling the net of doubt.

Having received the teacher’s enlightenment, Vasiṣṭha’s mind became clear; he submitted in silent admiration. The Master then sent him to another land, where his capacities were to evolve and transform as he taught. He received [the transmission].
He was instructed to perform a prostration and depart.
Regarding this, the *Fozu Tongzai* (General Record of the Buddhas and Patriarchs) states: "The First Patriarch Bodhidharma was the third son of King Xiangzhi of South India."
My son, when the King passed away, you left the household life and encountered the twenty-seventh patriarch, Prajñātāra. He transmitted the Great Dharma to you.

You then asked, "Now that I have received the Dharma, in which country should I go to transform [others]? Prajñātāra replied, "After you have received the Dharma, wait until more than sixty years after my parinirvāṇa;
you shall then go to the land of China to propagate the teachings. You asked, "Is there a vessel for the Dharma there who is capable of succeeding to our school?"
"Will there be any obstacles or difficulties for you a thousand years hence? Dharmatāra replied, "The number of those in the regions you have converted who shall attain Bodhi is beyond counting.
After my parinirvāṇa, there will be calamities during a kalpa; Wenbu will skillfully subdue them from within the waters.
When your time comes, you must not remain long in the south. Listen to my verse: 'While traveling on the road, crossing water, one encounters a sheep again. [Alone...]
He himself crossed the Yangtze River in sorrowful silence. Under the setting sun, a pair of elephants and horses were pitiable; two young trees had long flourished.
He further recited eight verses, all of which served as prophecies. After Śrīmitra passed away, he propagated the teachings in his native land.
At a time when his nephew, King Hsien-chien, was disparaging the Triple Gem, the Master dispatched his disciple P'o-lo-t'i (Purandara) to manifest supernatural powers and convert him.

He returned to his original course. As the Master’s karmic conditions had ripened in China, he immediately parted from his assembly. At that time, King Yijing (Wang Yi-jian) came in person to visit him, and the Master told him:
"You should diligently cultivate meritorious deeds and protect and uphold the Triple Gem. My departure is not too late; within nine months, I shall return.
The king wept and said, "Since you, my elder brother, have karmic ties there, you cannot be detained by me. I only pray that you will not forget your parents."
Upon completing his affairs in that country, he returned early. He then prepared a large ship and filled it with various treasures.
The King personally led his ministers and officials to escort him to the seashore, whereupon he reached Guangzhou.
The Record of the Manifestations and Transformations of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Part Two (End of Section Three)
